# #131 — Materialize current and short-term memory through OpenBrain lanes

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none

## Problem
OpenBrain already has session events and wraps, but the Hermes provider needs a stronger current-memory path so short-term state stays durable and fresh during active work. Current recall should not depend only on semantic search or old cached lane data.

## Scope
Use OpenBrain lanes as the durable short-term memory substrate for Hermes agents.

## Requirements
- Hermes provider should periodically update lane current_context_md via lane_upsert or an equivalent contract-safe tool.
- Current context should summarize active blockers, decisions, next actions, channel/thread context, and important recent events.
- append_session_event remains the append-only journal; current_context_md is the materialized working state.
- session_wrap remains the checkpoint before compaction/end.
- Outage behavior should spool/replay required OB writes without introducing another memory authority.
- Tests should prove current_context_md updates after turns/checkpoints and reloads after session switch/compaction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Active lane context can be refreshed and reloaded without raw transcript dumping.
- Short-term memory survives compaction/session restart through OB.
- Stale cache is not injected when lane context is expired or unavailable.
